parole.significato: A (walnut- or poppy-seed) roll (similar to Swiss roll) traditionally eaten in Hungary at Christmas time or at Easter.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Bavarian, compare Beugel, Beugl, Beigel (“a horseshoe-shaped walnut or poppy seed roll”), from German beugen (“to bend”). Suffixed with -i to resolve the word-final consonant cluster, compare cetli from Bavarian zettl or German Zettel (/⁠ˈt͡sɛtl̩⁠/) etc.
Borrowing from Bavarian zwider, from German zuwider (“against, antipathetic”).

parole.significato: backless kitchen stool, sometimes with a drawer for additional storage
parole.testo: From Bavarian hockerl (“small backless kitchen stool”), from German Hocker (“stool”) + -dli. Suffixed with -i to resolve the word-final consonant cluster, compare cetli from Bavarian zettl or German Zettel (/⁠ˈt͡sɛtl̩⁠/) etc.

parole.significato: hangman, executioner (the person who carries out the execution)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Bavarian hāher. Compare German Henker.

parole.significato: kohlrabi (variety of the cabbage, having a turnip-shaped edible stem)

Borrowed from Bavarian Keel (“Savoy cabbage”), from Latin caulis (“stem, stalk, cabbage”).

parole.significato: sloth (any mammal of the suborder Folivora)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps an internal development from dialectal lajha + -ár or borrowed from Bavarian laicher. First attested in 1604.

parole.significato: tank (a large cask or vat mounted on wheels, on a cart, or a truck; used to carry water, live fish, wine, must, or sila…
parole.testo: From Bavarian lait (“tank for carrying live fish”), from German leiten (“to lead, conduct”).

parole.significato: plump, chubby (having a full and rounded shape)
parole.testo: First attested in 1884. From Bavarian molet (“plump”), from German mollig, from Latin mollis (“soft”).

parole.significato: pelargonium (any of various flowering plants of the genus Pelargonium, commonly called geraniums)
parole.testo: First attested in 1858. From Bavarian [Term?], from German Muskat (“nutmeg”). Suffixed with -i to resolve the word-final consonant cluster, compare cetli from Bavarian zettl or German Zettel (/⁠ˈt͡sɛtl̩⁠/) etc.

parole.significato: baggage, luggage (bags and other containers that hold a traveller's belongings)
parole.testo: First attested in 1405. Borrowed from Bavarian malche.
From Bavarian nudl (“noodle”), of unknown origin. Suffixed with -i to resolve the word-final consonant cluster, compare cetli from Bavarian zettl or German Zettel (/⁠ˈt͡sɛtl̩⁠/) etc.
From the Bavarian baroke, from the Italian parrucca (“wig”).

parole.significato: paw, forepaw (soft foot of an animal)
parole.testo: From Bavarian [Term?], from German Pratze, Bratze (“paw, forepaw; large, coarse hand”), from Italian braccio (“arm”), from Latin brāchium, bracchium (“arm”), from Ancient Greek βρᾰχῑ́ων (brăkhī́ōn, “arm”). parole.significato: box, boxwood (any of various evergreen shrubs or trees of the genus Buxus)
parole.testo: First attested in 1525. Borrowed from Bavarian pukspam (German Buchsbaum).

parole.significato: marinade (seasoned mixture in which food is soaked to prepare it for cooking)
parole.testo: Most likely borrowed from Bavarian, or a back-formation from earlier pácol (“to marinate, to stain”). Compare Bavarian paiß, German Beize. First attested in 1787.

From Bavarian Bantl, diminutive of Pant (“ribbon”).

parole.significato: baker (person who bakes and sells bread, cakes, and similar items)
parole.testo: First attested in 1519. Borrowed from Bavarian beck.
From Bavarian paur (“farmer peasant”), from German bauen (“to build”).

parole.significato: phlegm (viscid mucus produced by the body, later especially mucus expelled from the bronchial passages by coughing)
parole.testo: From Bavarian šlāim, compare German Schleim (“viscous, thick juice, slime”). It is of Indo-European origin; compare Lithuanian sliẽkas (“earthworm”).

parole.significato: boom barrier, boom gate (a bar, or pole that can be lowered to block vehicular access through a controlled location, or…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Bavarian schrancpaum (compare the German compound Schranke (“gate, barrier”) + Baum (“tree”), as well as German Schlagbaum).

parole.significato: to squirt, spurt, splash, spray, jet
parole.testo: From Bavarian spritzen + -el (verb-forming suffix). First attested in 1896.
From Bavarian spröd, from German spröde (“brittle, rough”).
From Bavarian spuln, from German Spule (“spool”). Suffixed with -i to resolve the word-final consonant cluster, compare cetli from Bavarian zettl or German Zettel (/⁠ˈt͡sɛtl̩⁠/) etc.

From Bavarian sparen (“save up”) + -ol (verb-forming suffix). First attested in 1835.
From Bavarian Schaffer (“manager, bailiff”), from schaffen (“to create”).

parole.significato: shot, pellet (metal balls used as ammunition)
parole.testo: From Bavarian schrêd (plural), compare German Schrot.

parole.significato: wheelbarrow (a small, one-wheeled cart with handles at one end for transporting small loads)
parole.testo: First attested in 1876. From Bavarian tragatsch. The old vehicle sense is from [1956].
